• The seriousness of the trial process, including the directions of the judge, may help dispel
previously held myths.251

72. An observational study in late 2010 found that rape mythology was still heavily used by
defence counsel in trials.252 In 2019 research, over 80% of victim support respondents still
felt that myths are used frequently in court. Fifty-nine per cent of those surveyed as well as
78% of police lead respondents reported that such myths were infrequently or never
dispelled during the trials.253 The 2010 study identifies and comments on a wide range of
myths regarding what one would expect to happen before, during and after. The High Court
in Re A v B drew family judges’ attention to this chapter, indicating that those dealing with
family cases may also find the paragraphs around myths relevant and helpful.254 The 2010
study, and subsequent research referenced in the Law Commission’s paper on the view of
